newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Renong group down on steel firm talk.
newsitem.headline: Renong group down on steel firm talk.

text.p: Shares of companies belonging to Renong Bhd were lower on Thursday as rumours of its taking up a stake in the Philippines loss-making National Steel Corp resurfaced, analysts said.

Although the rumour of Renong's interest in the steel firm first surfaced in February, analysts now speculate that Renong's 53.9 percent-owned subsidiary, Cement Industries of Malaysia Bhd (CIMA), may be the vehicle for the acquisition.
At 0430 GMT, Renong slipped eight cents to 3.58 ringgit, United Engineers was down 40 cents to 19.20 and CIMA was down five to 6.95.
Officials at all three companies could not be immediately reached for comment.

"It is rumoured that Renong, via 53.9 percent-owned CIMA will acquire a majority stake, probably 69 percent to 84 percent, in National Steel Corporation of Philippines. This will probably be financed by a combination of rights issue and bank borrowings," said Thong and Kay Hian's head of research Laurence Lau in a daily report on Thursday.

"There would be no way that Renong could do it because they do not have the cash. CIMA is the only company in the group with the resources. But I don't understand the rationale (for the acquisition of National Steel)," said the head of research of a foreign brokerage house in Kuala Lumpur.
Malaysia's Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd had previously sold its 69.2 percent stake in National Steel in December to Hong Kong-based Hottick Investment Ltd for 12.17 billion pesos.
Analysts had said that National Steel's presence in Renong's stable would allow the infrastructure developer to expand its industrial base.
"I believe that National Steel can be turned around," said Lau.
